name: Hermes Agent
summary: Nous Research's open-source, terminal-oriented agent with skills, MCP integration, local execution, and a large Skills Hub ecosystem.
overview: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source agent for terminal, development, and multi-surface automation workflows. It should be treated as a major Agent page because its public ecosystem includes a GitHub repository, official documentation, and a large Skills Hub. The page should emphasize the difference between official docs, official/community skills, MCP integration, and local execution risk. Hermes is not just a small workflow concept; it is a full agent ecosystem that deserves the same source rigor as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Qwen Code, and OpenClaw.

strengths.title: Open-source agent repository
strengths.body: Hermes Agent has an official GitHub repository, making source review and ecosystem tracking possible.

strengths.title: Skills Hub ecosystem
strengths.body: The Skills Hub organizes hundreds of skills across software development, research, translation, productivity, DevOps, security, and other categories.

strengths.title: Terminal-first execution model
strengths.body: Hermes is best represented as a CLI-oriented agent where local execution, commands, and skill-driven workflows are central.

strengths.title: Nous Research positioning
strengths.body: The agent belongs to the broader Nous Research ecosystem, so model, agent, and skill materials should be labeled clearly.

extensionModel.label: CLI
extensionModel.body: Hermes should be mapped as a terminal-first agent surface with local command execution and interactive sessions.

extensionModel.label: Skills
extensionModel.body: The official Skills Hub is a core compatibility surface and should drive skill discovery, categorization, and review.

extensionModel.label: MCP
extensionModel.body: Hermes documentation positions MCP integration as part of the agent's extension story, but individual servers still need source review.

extensionModel.label: Workflow
extensionModel.body: Useful for local execution workflows, reusable skill packs, command patterns, and multi-agent or tool-connected routines.

recommendedStacks.title: Hermes Skills Hub review
recommendedStacks.body: Use the Skills Hub as the discovery source, but publish only skills that pass source, usefulness, and safety review.

recommendedStacks.title: CLI workflow kit
recommendedStacks.body: Map command packs and terminal workflows when they are backed by official docs or repository evidence.

recommendedStacks.title: MCP plus skill flow
recommendedStacks.body: Treat MCP servers as separate capability providers and connect them to Hermes only after compatibility evidence is clear.

limitations: The old placeholder documentation URL must not be used; Hermes pages should point to Nous Research docs and GitHub.
Large skill directories need safety and maintenance review before individual items are recommended.
Do not publish generated install commands; link to current official docs instead.
Compatibility with third-party skills or MCP servers must be verified per candidate.
